decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Arithmetic and Proportions

outcomes.description: Calculate with integers, fractions, decimals, and signed quantities.
Solve proportion, percentage, and unit-conversion problems.
Use bounds, scientific notation, and significant figures to check numerical claims.

includes: Exact arithmetic and numerical estimation

practice: Solve mixed quantitative problems and diagnose incorrect calculations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebra and Functions
decks.description: Manipulate symbolic models and their representations.

outcomes.description: Solve linear, quadratic, rational, and simple inequality problems while checking domains.
Translate among formulas, graphs, tables, compositions, and inverse functions.
Solve exponential and logarithmic models and interpret their parameters.
Calculate with complex numbers in Cartesian and polar notation.

includes: Symbolic fluency and elementary function families

practice: Build and check symbolic models from quantitative descriptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Geometry and Trigonometry

outcomes.description: Use similarity, coordinate distance, and angle relations to solve Euclidean measurement problems.
Derive and use unit-circle identities, radians, and sinusoidal representations.

includes: Plane geometry and computational trigonometry

practice: Solve geometric constructions and periodic-model problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Sets, Logic, and Proof

outcomes.description: Translate quantified statements and distinguish implications, converses, and negations.
Work with sets, relations, functions, equivalence classes, and countability examples.
Construct direct, contrapositive, contradiction, and counterexample arguments.
Prove recursive and integer-indexed claims using induction and strong induction.

includes: Informal set foundations and proof grammar

practice: Write complete proofs and repair invalid arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Data Literacy

outcomes.description: Calculate and interpret location, spread, proportions, and standardized differences.
Choose plots that expose distributions, relationships, and misleading scales.
Create a documented tabular dataset using a spreadsheet, handling units, missingness, and identifiers.

includes: Descriptive statistics and elementary spreadsheet operations
excludes: Formal hypothesis tests and causal identification

practice: Clean a small dataset and produce an auditable descriptive report.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra
decks.description: Compute and reason with linear structures.

outcomes.description: Solve linear systems by elimination and interpret rank and nullity.
Determine bases, coordinates, independence, and orthogonal projections.
Represent linear maps and change bases over real or complex scalars.
Compute eigendecompositions and singular-value decompositions and explain their applicability.

includes: Finite-dimensional theory with computational justification

practice: Solve matrix problems and justify geometric interpretations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and explain continuity using graphical and numerical evidence.
Differentiate elementary compositions and solve rate and optimization problems.
Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals and apply the fundamental theorem.
Test elementary series and use Taylor approximations with error estimates.

includes: Computational calculus and conceptual limit arguments
excludes: General epsilon-delta proofs and measure integration

practice: Solve modeling problems requiring method selection and error checks.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus

outcomes.description: Compute gradients, Jacobians, and Hessians and use local linearization.
Evaluate multiple integrals with coordinate changes and Jacobian factors.
Compute line and surface integrals and apply Green, Gauss, and Stokes theorems under their hypotheses.

includes: Curves, surfaces, partial derivatives, and integral theorems

practice: Solve field and geometry problems in multiple coordinate systems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Discrete Mathematics
decks.description: Prove and compute with finite structures.

outcomes.description: Derive counts using bijections, inclusion-exclusion, and generating functions.
Prove basic connectivity and tree properties and model problems with graphs.
Solve elementary recurrences and justify asymptotic growth bounds.

includes: Combinatorial proof and discrete models

practice: Write counting proofs and analyze discrete constructions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Elementary Number Theory

outcomes.description: Prove divisibility and prime-factorization claims using the Euclidean algorithm.
Solve modular equations using inverses, Euler's theorem, and the Chinese remainder theorem.
Establish solvability or impossibility for elementary Diophantine equations.

includes: Proof-based integer and modular arithmetic
excludes: Number fields and analytic prime distribution

practice: Construct proofs and implement small modular calculations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability

outcomes.description: Construct joint and conditional distributions and apply Bayes' rule with explicit sample spaces.
Transform discrete and continuous random variables and calculate their distributions.
Calculate moments, covariance, and conditional expectations in elementary models.
Justify elementary concentration bounds and select law-of-large-numbers or central-limit approximations.

includes: Discrete and density-based probability; introductory limit reasoning

practice: Derive distributions and compare exact probabilities with approximations.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Inference

outcomes.description: Construct estimators and confidence intervals and interpret repeated-sampling guarantees.
Choose and critique hypothesis tests with attention to power and multiplicity.
Fit linear and generalized linear models and diagnose residual and identifiability problems.
Compute posterior and predictive distributions in tractable Bayesian models.
Design randomized or blocked studies and distinguish sampling uncertainty from confounding.

includes: Applied frequentist and Bayesian inference
excludes: General asymptotic proofs and causal identification theory

practice: Analyze datasets and write assumption-sensitive inference reports.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Equations and Dynamics

outcomes.description: Solve standard first- and second-order equations and assess existence and uniqueness conditions.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure and interpret phase portraits.
Analyze equilibria, linearized stability, and elementary bifurcations of nonlinear systems.

includes: Analytic ODE methods and introductory dynamical systems
excludes: Weak PDE theory and stochastic differential equations

practice: Derive models, solve them, and compare phase portraits with trajectories.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis

outcomes.description: Separate conditioning, truncation, and floating-point error and derive basic error bounds.
Implement and compare direct and iterative linear solvers using residual and conditioning diagnostics.
Select interpolation, root-finding, and quadrature methods using convergence and smoothness assumptions.
Implement ODE time-stepping and analyze consistency, stability, and convergence.

includes: Numerical linear algebra, approximation, and ODE discretization

practice: Implement algorithms and conduct reproducible error-scaling experiments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis

outcomes.description: Prove sequence and function-series convergence claims, distinguishing pointwise and uniform convergence.
Prove continuity and compactness results in real and metric spaces.
Prove central differentiation and Riemann-integration theorems and justify exchanges of limits.

includes: Completeness, metric arguments, and rigorous calculus

practice: Write full proofs and construct counterexamples to weakened hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis

outcomes.description: Prove consequences of Cauchy's theorem and integral formula for holomorphic functions.
Classify isolated singularities and evaluate contour and real integrals by residues.
Analyze analytic continuation, branches, and conformal maps with explicit domains.

includes: Proof-based one-complex-variable analysis

practice: Prove analytic results and solve contour and mapping problems.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Group Theory

outcomes.description: Construct groups, homomorphisms, and quotients and prove the isomorphism theorems.
Use group actions and orbit-stabilizer arguments to solve classification and counting problems.
Apply Sylow theory and finite abelian group structure to determine possible groups.

includes: Proof-based group structure

practice: Prove structural results and classify small examples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Rings, Fields, and Galois Theory

outcomes.description: Analyze ideals, quotient rings, polynomial factorization, and principal or unique-factorization domains.
Compute degrees and minimal polynomials in algebraic field extensions.
Use the Galois correspondence to relate subgroup structure to solvability of equations.

includes: Ring and field proofs through finite Galois extensions

practice: Construct extensions and prove ring-theoretic claims.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: General Topology
decks.description: Reason about spaces independently of coordinates.

outcomes.description: Construct topologies and characterize continuity through open sets and convergence.
Prove compactness, connectedness, and separation results and identify counterexamples.
Analyze product, subspace, and quotient constructions using their defining properties.

includes: Point-set topology and examples

practice: Prove statements about constructed spaces and compare inequivalent notions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization Theory and Algorithms

outcomes.description: Prove convexity and use separation and duality to establish global bounds.
Derive first- and second-order conditions and apply KKT conditions with constraint qualifications.
Analyze gradient, Newton, and proximal methods under explicit convergence assumptions.

includes: Finite-dimensional smooth and convex optimization; linear programming duality

practice: Derive optimality systems and compare algorithms on controlled examples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure and Integration

outcomes.description: Construct measures from outer measures and analyze measurable functions and product spaces.
Construct the Lebesgue integral and prove central integral identities.
Apply and prove convergence, Fubini-Tonelli, and Radon-Nikodym results under their hypotheses.

includes: Measure construction, integration, and signed measures

practice: Write measure-theoretic proofs and counterexamples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure-Theoretic Probability

outcomes.description: Construct conditional expectation as a Radon-Nikodym derivative and prove its defining properties.
Distinguish modes of stochastic convergence and prove representative laws of large numbers and central-limit results.
Use stopping and convergence theorems for discrete-time martingales while checking integrability conditions.

includes: Probability spaces, independence, distributional limits, and martingales

practice: Prove limit and stopping results and identify failed hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis

outcomes.description: Prove and apply completeness, Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness, and open-mapping results.
Use Hilbert-space projection and representation theorems in function spaces.
Analyze bounded and compact operators and prove a compact self-adjoint spectral theorem.

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces; bounded-operator theory

practice: Prove existence and operator results in concrete function spaces.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Harmonic Analysis
decks.description: Develop Fourier analysis as function-space theory.

outcomes.description: Prove orthogonality, Plancherel, inversion, and representative Fourier convergence results.
Derive convolution inequalities and use approximate identities and maximal estimates to study convergence.
Define tempered distributions and calculate distributional Fourier transforms and derivatives.

includes: Fourier series and transforms with norm and convergence theory

practice: Prove transform theorems and construct convergence counterexamples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Sobolev Spaces and Weak PDEs

outcomes.description: Construct weak derivatives and prove basic Sobolev embedding, trace, and compactness results.
Derive variational formulations and prove elliptic existence and uniqueness using coercivity.
Establish energy estimates for evolution equations and distinguish weak existence from regularity.

includes: Sobolev theory; weak elliptic, parabolic, and wave models

practice: Write existence proofs and compare weak and classical solutions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry

outcomes.description: Construct smooth manifolds, tangent bundles, and coordinate-independent tensor fields.
Compute exterior derivatives and integrals of forms and prove the manifold Stokes theorem.
Calculate connections, geodesics, and curvature for Riemannian and pseudo-Riemannian metrics.

excludes: Geometric analysis and global classification research

practice: Compute invariant quantities and prove coordinate-independence claims.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology

Construct chain complexes and compute homology using exact sequences and cellular methods.

decks.title: Category Theory

Construct natural transformations and apply the Yoneda lemma to concrete representability problems.

practice: Prove universal properties and translate constructions between examples.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Homological Algebra

outcomes.description: Construct modules, tensor products, and projective or injective resolutions.

practice: Construct resolutions and prove exact-sequence arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Number Theory

practice: Calculate in explicit number fields and prove structural results.

decks.title: Mathematical Logic

outcomes.description: Construct first-order structures and distinguish satisfaction, derivability, and elementary equivalence.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Processes

decks.subject: mathematics

practice: Prove estimator properties and construct failure examples.

decks.subject: mathematics

scopeIssues: The proposal does not yet supply sufficiently explicit graduate chemistry outcomes for advanced reaction dynamics, modern inorganic electronic-structure theory, and multivariate chemometrics. Their neighboring introductory and computational treatments do not establish those capabilities; additional deck specifications and coverage rows are needed before accepting whole-field chemistry coverage.

Mathematics still needs explicit coverage decisions and substantive outcomes for analytic number theory, advanced combinatorics, and a graduate continuation of numerical PDE discretization. Existing number theory, discrete mathematics, and weak PDE outcomes do not teach those branches.

Computer-science coverage needs an explicit reinforcement-learning route with Markov decision processes, Bellman theory, exploration, and off-policy evaluation. The included planning, probabilistic inference, and robotics outcomes do not substitute for its foundations.

Several important scope boundaries remain insufficiently reconciled at domain-and-depth level, including advanced quantum information, open quantum systems, and graduate evolutionary theory beyond the included population-genetic and evo-devo routes. These require explicit inclusion or justified specialist-extension decisions rather than assumed coverage.
practiceNotes: Flashcards support retrieval and discrimination; programming competence, proof construction, experimental technique, and research judgment require the extended practice specified in each deck.

Chemical, biological, and physical experiments require appropriate supervision, local risk assessment, facility procedures, and approved waste handling. These conditions are proposed requirements, not represented as satisfied.

Radioactive sources, high-power equipment, cryogens, lasers, and regulated biological materials require facility-specific training and authorization. Supplied datasets and simulations provide alternatives where access is unavailable.
Human-participant, animal, field-collection, and sensitive genomic work may require institutional ethics approval, consent, permits, privacy safeguards, and data-use agreements.
Security practice must use owned or explicitly authorized systems. Cryptographic exercises are educational implementations, not deployment recommendations.
Embedded and robotics practice should begin in simulation or with supervised low-voltage, low-energy hardware; educational performance does not establish safety certification.
Drug-discovery, epidemiological, and physiological exercises do not authorize clinical treatment, prescribing, or operational public-health decisions.
